text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called the "silent killer" because it typically causes no signs or symptoms. A person can have high blood pressure for years without realizing it while it quietly damages the heart, brain, and kidneys.
snippet_highlighted_words: typically causes no signs or symptoms

text_blocks.snippet: The only reliable way to know if you have high blood pressure is to have it measured by a healthcare provider or with a validated home monitor.
When Symptoms Do Appear (Dangerously High Blood Pressure)
Symptoms generally only show up if blood pressure becomes extremely high—a condition known as severe hypertension or a hypertensive crisis (readings above 180/120 mm Hg).
Potential warning signs during severe spikes include:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Vision changes (such as blurred or double vision)
Fatigue or feeling exhausted from the heart working harder

text_blocks.snippet: What to Do If Blood Pressure Is Very High (>180/120 mm Hg)

list.snippet: Wait 1 minute and retest: If your reading is 180/120 mm Hg or higher, rest for a minute and check it a second time.

If you have symptoms: Call 911 immediately if a reading above 180/120 mm Hg is accompanied by chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, vision changes, or trouble speaking (signs of a hypertensive emergency).
If you do not have symptoms: Contact your doctor right away for guidance on adjusting or starting medication.
